title: Morn of Beauty, Joyous Morn
description: Morn of Beauty, Joyous Morn in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Morn of beau-ty, joy-ous morn, Hails the Re-sur-rec-tion Day, All our fears are borne a-way, Hope in-to our world is born.

lines: Morn of beauty, joyous morn,
Hails the Resurrection Day,
All our fears are borne away,
Hope into our world is born.
See, the stone is rolled away;
Empty stands the silent tomb,
Death is dead, and gone the gloom
Where the risen Saviour lay.
Women bear the spices, sad,
In the early morning grey,
But they wiped their tears away,
For the angel made them glad.
Tell the tidings far abroad,
"He is risen even as He said,"
Life immortal from the dead
Is the gift of Christ our God.
Glory, glory evermore,
To the Christ who died to save,
Wresting victory from the grave,
To the Christ we now adore.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
